Hannah —

Thanks for taking this. As part of NebulaSoft's procurement intake for our LLM inference platform evaluation we need a more granular breakdown of how Redwood would map our peak/sustained throughput targets to reserved capacity. Specifically we need:

- GPU SKU mapping (H100 / A100 / L4 equivalents) and per-GPU steady-state throughput for our workload (see attached RFP scope).
- Suggested reservation slotting (how many reserved "slots" and what GPU family per slot).
- Expected p50/p95 token latency estimates at steady-state and under 3x burst.
- Recommended burst policy and how burst billing / overage would work.
- Any fallback SKUs you would auto-route to if our preferred GPUs aren't available.

Targets: sustained ~2,000,000 tokens/day, peak day ~6,000,000 tokens/day, average request size ~320 tokens, 95th pct request size ~2,048 tokens. We plan to start in us-west with a pilot of 4 production routes.

Can you send a detailed worksheet and a short note describing recommended reservation sizing? Ideally by end of week so procurement can include it in our decision pack.

Regards,

Artem —

Thanks, attaching a workbook (nebula_dedicated_workbook_v1.xlsx) with a throughput decomposition and a recommended starting reservation. Summary below; workbook has the assumptions and per-route rows.

Key assumptions (see workbook tab "Assumptions"):
- Model family: mixture of medium instruction-tuned 13B and smaller quantized 7B variants.
- Avg request 320 tokens, p95 2,048 tokens. Effective tokens/day translated to sustained tokens/sec and average concurrency observed.
- Latency targets: p50 <150 ms, p95 budget <800 ms for normal traffic (pilot routes).

GPU SKU throughput (approximate, representative for Redwood runtime + sequence length distribution):
- H100 80GB (fp16/bf16): ~220 tokens/sec per GPU for 13B-class fine-tuned models (seq512 scenario).
- A100 40GB (fp16): ~150 tokens/sec per GPU for same workload.
- L4 48GB (int8 quantized): ~600 tokens/sec for compact 7B-class quantized models (best for embedding/low-latency small models).

Recommended starter reservation (sustained target mapping):
- Sustained target 2,000,000 tokens/day = ~23.15 tokens/sec average across 24h.
- Real scheduling overhead & peak spikes require headroom; we map to sustained concurrent effective tokens/sec of ~350 tokens/sec for the production routes during business hours.
- Mapping (convert to GPU equivalents):
  - Option A (High-performance): 2 x H100 (2 * 220 = 440 tps) — comfortable headroom for sustained + short bursts; good p95 margin.
  - Option B (Balanced cost): 3 x A100 (3 * 150 = 450 tps) — slightly more instances, cost-effective if A100 SKUs are preferred.
  - Option C (Mixed): 1 H100 + 2 L4 + 1 A100 (mixed pool) — gives flexibility across model sizes and allows low-latency small-model routing to L4s for cost savings.

Burst policy recommendation:
- Allow application-level burst up to 3x of reserved capacity for short windows (<=10 minutes) via auto-burst to shared pool or region fallback. We suggest a burst cap of 3x with pre-negotiated overage rate. Workbook includes cost delta rows.

Fallback SKUs and routing rules:
- Primary: H100 (if committed); Fallback: A100 (equivalent performance band).
- For small models, route to L4 if available — reduces cost and improves tail-latency for short requests.

Next steps / deliverables we attached:
- nebula_dedicated_workbook_v1.xlsx (per-route slotting, tokens/sec assumptions, cost delta estimates).
- Proposed cadence: 4-week pilot with measurement-driven slotting adjustments, canary traffic for first 48 hours.

Let us know a good time for a 30-min slot to walk through the workbook.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0147
